title: Check Digitorial Permutation
summary: Given an integer n, check if any permutation of its digits (excluding permutations starting with zero) forms a digitorial number.
statement: Given an integer n, check if any permutation of its digits (excluding permutations starting with zero) forms a digitorial number. A digitorial number is one where the sum of the factorials of its digits equals the number itself. Return true if such a permutation exists, otherwise return false. Factorial of x (x!) is the product of all positive integers up to x, with 0! defined as 1.
constraints: n is a positive integer with at most seven decimal digits.
Permutations with a leading zero are not valid integers.
Return whether some permutation equals the sum of the factorials of its own digits.
hints: Permuting digits never changes the multiset of digits or their factorial sum.
Compute that invariant sum once, then compare its digits with the input digits.
Equal sorted digit sequences prove the sum is a permutation without enumerating arrangements.
If a valid permutation exists it must equal the fixed factorial sum; conversely equal digit multisets provide that permutation, and a positive integer has no leading-zero representation.
editorial: If a valid permutation exists it must equal the fixed factorial sum; conversely equal digit multisets provide that permutation, and a positive integer has no leading-zero representation.

tests.explanation: 145 equals 1!+4!+5!, so its own digit order is a valid digitorial.
Reordering the digits as 145 produces a digitorial, so the answer is true.
